items.title: IPO fundraising rises 30% to record ₹84,400 crore in H1FY27: Report
items.summary:
India's mainboard IPO market witnessed a record fund mobilisation at Rs 84,400 crore in the first half of FY27, registering a 30 per cent rise over the year-ago period, with nearly 94 per cent of the funds raised during the July-September period, according to a report by Grant Thornton Bharat.
As many as 71 companies made their stock market debut during April-September 2026, compared with 55 in the corresponding period a year ago.
According to the report, the funds raised increased from Rs 64,900 crore in H1 FY26 to Rs 84,400 crore in H1 FY27.
The average listing-day gains improved to 18 per cent from 10 per cent a year ago, while average retail oversubscription increased to 28 times from 25 times, the report titled 'India IPO Market: H1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 Review' said.
Notably, September was the busiest month, with 32 IPOs collectively raising Rs 40,400 crore.
In terms of sectoral contribution, financial services accounted for 43 per cent of the total capital mobilised during H1 FY
